record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; artifact contents and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports difference-in-means directions from residual activations and an ablation result on safety refusal, directly testing removal of a refusal direction. The reported extraction and ablation resemble the original method, though the README does not establish the original all-layer/all-position intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for safety ablation, safety-versus-epistemic direction geometry, and an epistemic probe. Setup commands and pipeline descriptions without reported outcomes are not rows. The README names additional artifact files, but their contents are unavailable here.
record.test_reason: It extracts a difference-in-means safety direction from harmful (AdvBench) minus benign (Alpaca) prompts in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It then ablates that direction and reports the safety refusal rate (0.98 to 0.16), a direct test of V1's ablation claim. The intervention scope (layers, positions) is not stated, and the model was run in 4-bit.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that safety refusal and epistemic abstention are separate directions, not one shared dominant direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means directions and behavioral ablation, but the README does not establish the original full all-layer/all-position intervention or report addition and capability results. This repository is a research pipeline/tool with checked-in result artifacts; it is not identified as a reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The Llama safety-versus-epistemic cosine varies across layers: the README reports a mean across layers and a maximum at model.layers.20. Cross-family cosine values are also reported at each model's top safety layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-refusal and epistemic-abstention directions are nearly orthogonal: Llama mean cosine 0.049, max 0.183; Qwen3 -0.039; Gemma-2 0.123.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety refusal and epistemic abstention ('I don't know') use geometrically distinct directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety ablation raises epistemic abstention slightly, from 0.82 to 0.88.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating the refusal direction does not suppress epistemic abstention.

fits_no_version.finding: An epistemic probe reaches 1.00 held-out accuracy at layer 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Answerable versus unanswerable questions are linearly separable in activations.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop poster (accepted; as stated in README)
record.problems: Only README summaries are available; the underlying result artifacts and methods were not inspected. The README does not state uncertainty values for the reported results or specify the layer and intervention scope for the strongest ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional README-reported numerical outcomes were available beyond those listed. The README mentions quantization and other artifacts, but gives no corresponding numerical findings in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; general capability after ablation; ablation at all layers and positions; ablation results for Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2-9B (only cosines are reported for these).

missing.what: Quantization drift of the safety direction under NF4, INT8, GPTQ and AWQ (fig3, quantization sweep artifact); no numbers are in the README.
Full cross-ablation sweep across layers and strengths, including epistemic-direction ablation's effect on safety refusal, with bootstrap CIs.
Preprint text with the methods, including the ablation scope.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available. The V1 evidence is one best-of-sweep number on a 4-bit model, with no capability check and no uncertainty in the README (although bootstrap CIs are computed per the pipeline). The study's main question, safety versus epistemic separation, bears on no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report adding the direction, effects on general capability, or an ablation at every layer and position.
No reported result for a weight edit or abliteration.
No reported result testing whether attacks suppress the direction or training against its ablation adds robustness.
The README compares safety-refusal and epistemic-abstention directions, but does not test whether safety refusal itself is affine, conical, or distributed across multiple directions.
No separate measurement of a harmfulness judgment and a refusal decision.
Cross-family comparisons are reported, but the README does not test whether the same refusal direction transfers across languages, model variants, or training stages.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
